preconditions.expression: T == int(stdin.split()[0]) and T >= 1 and T <= 10
preconditions.description: T is the number of test cases, where 1 ≤ T ≤ 10.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= N <= 15 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit() and (N := int(line.split()[0])) >= 1 and N <= 15)
preconditions.description: For each test case, N is the number of vertices, where 1 ≤ N ≤ 15.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= M < (N * (N - 1) // 2) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and line.split()[1].isdigit() and (M := int(line.split()[1])) >= 0 and M < (N * (N - 1) // 2))
preconditions.description: For each test case, M is the number of edges, where 0 ≤ M < N*(N-1)/2.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= X <= N and 1 <= Y <= N for line in stdin.splitlines()[2:] if line.strip() and line.split() and (X := int(line.split()[0])) >= 1 and X <= N and (Y := int(line.split()[1])) >= 1 and Y <= N)
preconditions.description: For each edge, X and Y are valid vertex indices, where 1 ≤ X, Y ≤ N.

postconditions.expression: all(' '.join(map(str, (x, y))) in stdout.splitlines() for (x, y) in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is a line containing two integers x and y (space-separated) representing the minimal solution to the equation A * x = B * y, where A is the minimum S[i] and B is the maximum S[i].

postconditions.expression: all(x >= 1 and y >= 1 for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip() and (x := int(line.split()[0])) >= 1 and (y := int(line.split()[1])) >= 1)
postconditions.description: The values of x and y are positive integers.

postconditions.expression: all((A := min(S)) > 0 and (B := max(S)) > 0 and (A * x == B * y) for S in [compute_S(N, edges) for N, edges in parse_test_cases(stdin)] for (x, y) in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()])
postconditions.description: The output (x, y) satisfies the equation A * x = B * y, where A is the minimum S[i] and B is the maximum S[i], and S[i] is computed as the maximum sum of vertices in the longest simple path ending at vertex i.
